To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1)  M. truncatula accession and AMF treatment had significant effects on plant physiology and gene expression, and (2)  M. trunctula accessions varied in their response to AMF colonization.
the effects of AMF on physiological and molecular responses varied across diverse M. truncatula accesssions.
the diverse accessions of M. trunchula varied in their response to AMF inoculation and that some accessions were larger, had higher gs and higher Lo when colonized by the AMF Funeliformis mosseaae.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of intraspecific plant diversity in mediating the effects of AMF on plant water relations.
the role of plant intraspecific variability in response to AMF inoculation and the underlying mechanisms of these responses, and is the first study to examine these questions in M. trucatula.
how plant diversity and AMF can interact to impact on plant water use, and how these interactions can be linked with physiological and molecular measures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the responses to F. mossea e inoculation varied across the accessions and that the variation in responses was associated with variation in gene expression.
the effects of AMF inoculation on physiological responses are highly variable, and that this is associated with variation in the molecular responses to AMF.
the effects of AMF inoculation are highly dependent on plant intraspecific genetic diversity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of AMF colonization were variable across accessions and that the effects were more apparent when measured as physiological traits rather than molecular traits.

M. trucatula intraspecific diversity can have variable effects on physiology and gene expression in response to AMF inoculation, and that these effects can have important consequences for plant water relations.
AMF colonization can increase plant water relations, but this response is variable, and the response of a given genotype to a given treatment can be predicted by its response to other treatments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of AMF on plant water relations vary with both the AMF species and the plant genotype.
the effects of AMF colonization on plant water relations vary across genotypes, but that the molecular mechanisms underlying such responses are conserved.
M. trucatula intraspecific diversity is important for studying plant–AMF interactions and that these interactions are complex, with both physiological and molecular components.
